raw_response:
I've been farming these 10 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I'm 62 now, and it's just my wife and me working the land most days — our son works in a factory in the county town and only comes back for harvest. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bags and do my own cost sums, but I learned how to farm by doing it and watching the older farmers around me. If Lao Zhang's wheat looks greener than mine, I go ask him what he spread on his field. That's how I get my information.

Last year my wheat made about 500 jin per mu, the maize made about 600 jin, and the cotton gave about 250 jin of seed cotton. This year I will stick close to that — change is risky, and I know these numbers cover my costs.

For the 8 mu that rotates wheat and maize: I sowed wheat last October with an improved variety I've been saving seed from for three years now. It germinates well and I trust it. Before sowing I ran the rotary tiller twice to chop up the maize stalks. For basal fertilizer I spread 80 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu — that's from the dealer in town, costs about 180 yuan for a 50kg bag. In March, at green-up, I will topdress with 50 jin of urea per mu — urea is about 110 yuan a bag now. I will irrigate that wheat three times: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I'll spray twice — herbicide right after sowing, and one insecticide-fungicide mix if I see aphids or rust.

After wheat harvest in early June, I will plant hybrid maize the same day without ploughing — there's no time to waste before the summer heat. I put 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the furrow with the seed, more than wheat because maize needs a strong start. When the plants are knee-high, I cultivate between rows and side-dress 50 jin of urea per mu. I will irrigate twice: one good watering if June is dry, and one at tasseling in July. Two sprays: herbicide before emergence, and one for armyworm if I spot them in August.

For the 2.1 mu of cotton: Cotton is fussy and needs work. I deep-plough that plot in April with my small tractor. I plant Bt hybrid cotton — everyone here switched to Bt years ago, the bollworm can't kill it. Basal fertilizer is 100 jin of compound per mu. I side-dress twice with urea, 30 jin per mu each time — once when the seedlings have four true leaves, and again at first flower. At flowering I also spread 40 jin of potassium sulfate per mu because cotton drinks potash; without enough the bolls drop and you get nothing. I will irrigate three times: at budding, at peak flower, and at boll stage. I will spray five times — even Bt cotton gets aphids, spider mites, and blight. Last year I stopped at four sprays and the mites cost me yield.

I have a well so I pump water when I need it, but the electricity meter spins fast. Three times for wheat, two for maize, three for cotton — that's what I did last year and it was enough. I know fertilizer prices went up again, but I would rather put in a bit too much than risk too little. A bad harvest means I lose my shirt; wasting 20 jin of fertilizer is just a few yuan down the drain. I watch what the neighbors do. If everyone around here puts 50 jin of urea on their maize, I put 50 jin too. I'm not going to be the only one trying to save money and end up with the shortest stalks in the village.
